iconic_games_note: Genuinely rich football venue (not an NFL-bowl site): hosted the 2010 Copa Libertadores Final first leg, eight 2011 FIFA U-17 World Cup matches (incl. a semifinal), and the full football tournament + ceremonies of the 2011 Pan American Games. For WC2026 it hosts four group-stage matches only — the only 2026 venue with no knockout games. As of 2026-06-23 two group matches have been played (KOR 2–1 CZE on 11 Jun; MEX 1–0 KOR on 18 Jun); the remaining two (Colombia vs DR Congo, 23 Jun; Uruguay vs Spain, 26 Jun) had not yet been played and have no scores. The venue also staged Pathway 1 of the March 2026 inter-confederation play-offs. NOTE: the 30 Jul 2010 Man Utd friendly was the stadium's THIRD public match per the cited source, not the inaugural/opening match.

city_history.founded: Guadalajara was founded 14 February 1542 in the Atemajac Valley (after several earlier relocations from 1532); became capital of Nueva Galicia in 1560.
city_history.significance: Capital and most populous city of the state of Jalisco; its metropolitan area (~5.3 million, 2020) is the third-largest in Mexico. Often called the 'most Mexican of Mexican cities' — heartland of mariachi, tequila, charrería and Ballet Folklórico. The WC2026 venue is in the suburb of Zapopan, part of the Guadalajara metropolitan area.
city_history.football_culture: Football culture centres on C.D. Guadalajara (Chivas), founded 1906 and one of Mexico's two most popular and successful clubs — famous for fielding only Mexican players. Chivas, tenant of Estadio Akron, is woven into the city's identity. The metro also hosts Liga MX side Atlas; the city previously staged matches at the historic Estadio Jalisco (a 1970 & 1986 World Cup venue) before Chivas built this stadium in 2010.

stadium_history_facts: Construction announced February 2004 (Chivas intended to leave the historic Estadio Jalisco); ground broken May 2007 after financing delays.

Opened 30 July 2010; an early high-profile friendly (the stadium's third public match per Wikipedia) was C.D. Guadalajara 3–2 Manchester United, with the first goal at the stadium scored by Javier 'Chicharito' Hernández for Guadalajara.

Concept design by Jean-Marie Massaud & Daniel Pouzet; sports architecture by Populous (formerly HOK Sport); architect of record VFO. Spherical/coliseum form built into a raised, grass-covered artificial hill (berm) wrapping the back of the stands.
Original construction cost reported as US$200 million by Wikipedia (≈US$295m in 2025 dollars); some other sources (StadiumDB) cite a lower figure — original cost is contested.
Opened with artificial turf, which drew heavy player criticism; replaced with natural grass in mid-2012.
Name history: Estadio Omnilife (2010–2016) → Estadio Chivas (2016–2017) → Estadio Akron from December 2017 (deal with lubricants firm Grupo Akron).
Home of C.D. Guadalajara since 2010 and used for selected Mexico national team matches.

Hosted the 2010 Copa Libertadores Final (1st leg), the 2011 Pan American Games opening/closing ceremonies + full football tournament, and 8 matches of the 2011 FIFA U-17 World Cup (incl. a semifinal).
For WC2026, temporarily renamed 'Estadio Guadalajara' per FIFA's clean-venue policy; hosts 4 group-stage matches and is the only 2026 venue with no knockout games.
